items.title: CISA adds two actively exploited Zammad vulnerabilities to danger list — update your software now at zammad.org
items.summary: CISA added Zammad Session Fixation (CVE-2026-102489) and Improper Privilege Management (CVE-2026-102490) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 2. If your organization uses Zammad helpdesk software, update immediately at zammad.org. Federal agencies have until October 11 to patch.

items.title: Windows 11 has a free built-in ransomware shield — Controlled Folder Access stops file encryption in seconds
items.summary: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Manage ransomware protection > turn on Controlled folder access. Free, built into Windows 11, protects Documents, Pictures, Desktop folders automatically. Allow trusted apps if they get blocked.

items.title: Clay Electric outage texts tell you the power is out before your neighbor knows — free at clayelectric.com
items.summary: Sign up for free outage alerts at clayelectric.com or text OUT to 855-939-3840. Get real-time text/email alerts the moment power goes out at your address. The MyClayElectric app also shows a live outage map.

items.title: Windows 11 24H2 loses security updates October 13 — check your version at Settings > System > About and upgrade free
items.summary: Open Settings > System > About > check Windows version. If you're on 24H2 Home/Pro, go to Settings > Windows Update and upgrade to 25H2. Free, automatic, keeps you protected. Deadline is tomorrow, October 13.

items.title: Windows 11 Storage Sense automatically frees 5-50 GB monthly — turn it on in Settings > System > Storage
items.summary: Open Settings > System > Storage > turn on Storage Sense. Windows automatically deletes temp files, empties Recycle Bin, and cleans Downloads folder on a schedule you set. Free, built-in, no download needed. Runs when disk space is low or daily/weekly/monthly.

items.title: Fake Virus Popup Scam
items.summary:
That "Virus Detected" Popup Is a Total Fake.

You're browsing the web and suddenly a loud siren blares from your speakers. A giant red popup fills the screen: "WARNING: 47 VIRUS DETECTED. Your files are being stolen. Call Microsoft Support NOW: 1-888-XXX-XXXX."

Here's the truth: Microsoft doesn't work this way. That popup is a webpage — just a picture. It can't see your files. It can't hurt anything. It's a lie.

items.title: Fake hurricane charity scams targeting Floridians — report free at ReportFraud.ftc.gov
items.summary:
CISA and the FTC warn: scammers pose as hurricane charities after every storm. Never donate via gift card, crypto, or wire transfer. Verify charities at Give.org or CharityNavigator.org, and report scams free at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

items.title: Firefox 157.0.1 warns when something is reading your encrypted traffic — free update at firefox.com
items.summary: Firefox 157.0.1 adds a new shield icon warning when software on your PC (like corporate monitoring tools or malware) intercepts your encrypted web traffic. Update free at firefox.com or use the built-in updater (Menu → Help → About Firefox).

items.title: Windows Update Triggers a Crash — The October Patch is Here
items.summary: Microsoft confirmed this week that a October 2026 Windows update can cause some programs and games to crash when they play certain sound files. The problem only hits a narrow set of audio paths — not every machine — but if you installed updates in the last 48 hours and noticed sudden crashes, that's likely it. Don't reinstall anything, don't roll back your drivers, and don't call support yet. Microsoft is shipping a fix in the next update, expected within days. The honest answer is that these bugs are real, they're temporary, and the correct move is to wait for the patch rather than chase the problem with a new install.

items.title: Apple just shipped a new iPhone security update that closes a flaw people were already attacked with — install it free at Settings > General > Software Update
items.summary: Pick up your iPhone, open Settings → General → Software Update, and tap Update Now. Apple's newest security update fixes a hole that has already been used in real attacks against real people, not just a theoretical problem. It takes about 10 minutes on Wi-Fi and it's completely free. Do it tonight.

items.title: Speed up a sluggish Windows PC for free with Microsoft PC Manager — Microsoft's own one-click cleaner, at pcmanager.microsoft.com
items.summary: Download Microsoft PC Manager free from pcmanager.microsoft.com or from the Microsoft Store (search "Microsoft PC Manager"). Open it and click Cleanup — it sweeps out junk files, shows you which programs are slowing your startup, and runs Microsoft's own virus scan, all from one window. No subscription, no account needed, and no pop-up ads after every click.
